# Headless UI verification (no browser, no root)

You cannot judge a UI from its HTML. This is how to actually see it, and how to
back "readable" with a number instead of an opinion.

## 1. Get a working Chromium without root (WSL)

Playwright's Chromium usually fails with `error while loading shared libraries:
libnspr4.so` because the NSS/NSPR runtime libs are missing, and `sudo apt install`
needs a password you must not ask for. Unpack the debs into your home instead:

```bash
mkdir -p ~/.local/chromium-libs /tmp/kbdeb && cd /tmp/kbdeb
apt-get download libnspr4 libnss3        # works unprivileged
for d in *.deb; do dpkg-deb -x "$d" ~/.local/chromium-libs/; done
LIBS=~/.local/chromium-libs/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu
ldd $(ls -d ~/.cache/ms-playwright/chromium-*/chrome-linux64/chrome | tail -1) | grep -c 'not found'   # expect 0
```

## 2. Screenshot

Use `scripts/screenshot.sh <url> <out.png> [w] [h]`, or by hand:

```bash
CH=$(ls -d ~/.cache/ms-playwright/chromium-*/chrome-linux64/chrome | tail -1)
LD_LIBRARY_PATH=$LIBS $CH --headless=old --no-sandbox --disable-gpu --no-first-run \
  --disable-dev-shm-usage --hide-scrollbars --virtual-time-budget=3000 \
  --window-size=1400,3600 --screenshot=/tmp/shot.png "http://127.0.0.1:8790/?theme=dark"
```

Rules that matter:
* `--headless=old`. Plain `--headless` (new) hangs until the command times out here.
* `--virtual-time-budget=3000` so JS/DOM is settled before the capture.
* Oversize `--window-size` for a full-page look; a capture never scrolls.
* Control light/dark from the page (`?theme=dark`), not from CLI flags: emulating
  `prefers-color-scheme` from the command line is unreliable, and `--force-dark-mode`
  also repaints the page (auto-dark), so what you see is not the CSS you wrote.
* Windows `chrome.exe` under `/mnt/c/...` also renders and screenshots, but on this
  machine it produced colours that did not match the page's own CSS - never judge
  colour from it.
* Look at the PNG with `vision_analyze`; for a long page pass `region=[x1,y1,x2,y2]`
  (original pixels) to inspect the lower half at full resolution.

## 3. Back "readable" with numbers

WCAG 2.2 AA floors: 4.5:1 normal text, 3:1 large text and non-text marks
(WCAG 1.4.11: borders, focus rings, status dots). GitHub's Primer team checks every
foreground/background pair with a script on every change rather than by eye.
Copy that: keep a small checker that mirrors the token values used by the UI
(see `tools/kb-ui-contrast-check.py` beside the knowledge-base UIs) and run it after
every colour edit; it must exit non-zero on failure.

Failures this catches in practice:
* `color-scheme: light dark` declared with **no explicit background** - on a dark-mode
  host the browser paints a dark canvas under the page's near-black text.
* secondary greys picked ad hoc (`#9ca3af` on white = 2.2:1), and `opacity: .55`
  stacked on top of an already-low-contrast grey.
* `white` on mid-green/red buttons (4.5:1 needs a darker fill: `#1a7f37`, `#238636`).

## 4. Design rules worth copying (published practice)

* GitHub Primer: one semantic role per token (`canvas`, `canvas.subtle`, `fg.default`,
  `fg.muted`, `border.muted`, `accent`) - never a raw hex at a call site.
* Radix Colors 12-step discipline: 1-2 backgrounds, 3-5 component surfaces
  (3 normal / 4 hover / 5 pressed), 6-8 borders (6 subtle / 7 interactive / 8 focus),
  9-10 solid fills (9 normal / 10 hover), 11-12 text (11 muted / 12 high contrast).
  Text comes in exactly two weights, not an improvised grey per component.
* Status is never colour alone: every chip carries a dot AND a label, so state
  survives greyscale printing and colour-vision deficiency.
* Set `background` explicitly on `body`; do not let the UA decide.
* Toggle pattern that works for local tools: system preference by default, a corner
  button writing `localStorage`, `data-theme` on `<html>` for the override, and a
  `?theme=` URL param for screenshots.

## 5. Verify the served page, not just the file

Templates can render fine while the running service still serves the old CSS.
After a restart: `curl -s -o /tmp/x.html -w '%{http_code}' URL` and `grep -c` for a
new class name; count interactive elements (`grep -c 'data-*'`) to confirm a rewrite
kept them; for a gated page also check the 403 path.

## 6. This machine's knowledge-base UIs

* Read-only dashboard: `http://127.0.0.1:8790/`, source `tools/intelligence-dashboard.py`.
* Approval console: `http://127.0.0.1:8795/?t=<token>`, source
  `tools/intelligence-approval-console.py`; token lives in
  `~/.local/state/intelligence-layer/console.env` (never print it, never put it in chat).
* Both are systemd user units: `systemctl --user restart kb-dashboard kb-approval-console`.
* Source files sit in `/mnt/d/OpenClaw/tools/` (not a git repo); the rendered
  `/mnt/d/intelligence-layer/dashboard.html` is gitignored.
* Colour tokens are mirrored in `tools/kb-ui-contrast-check.py` - update both
  together or the check stops meaning anything. Backups of the previous UI are kept
  as `*.bak-<timestamp>` next to the scripts.
* Restyling must not touch the approval path: the token check, the cookie, the POST
  field names (`kind`/`id`/`decision`/`reason`) and "only a human approves" stay as
  they are. The console shells out to the human-owned approve/reject tools; keep it
  that way.
